newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends higher on silver, short covering.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends higher on silver, short covering.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended firmer on Thursday from New York's previous close, buoyed by short covering and strong silver, but the upside was met by selling interest which prevented solid gains, traders said.
Bullion ended at US$341.30/80 an ounce against New York's US$341.00/50 close on Wednesday.
"We saw good buying interest in silver from the Middle East after our lunch hour and gold tried to follow that," said one precious metals trader.
Other dealers reported marginal physical demand and shortcovering which helped pull gold up.
Selling interest from London in the afternoon at around $342 per ounce capped gains, dealers said, but noted that a relatively strong performance in the white metals could help keep gold up.
Local gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,162 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from its previous fix at -5.00.
